headline: Brent Crude Holds Near $92.60 per Barrel as Middle East Risk Premium Sustains Prices
summary: Brent crude futures traded around $92.67 per barrel while WTI crude reached $83.61. Prices remained supported by geopolitical risk premiums from Middle East shipping and refinery attacks despite signs of abundant global crude supply.
why: Brent crude is the global benchmark for international oil pricing, influencing global energy sector profitability and inflation.

impacts.name: Brent Crude
impacts.why: Brent crude prices stabilized as supply concerns were balanced by Middle East geopolitical risks.
